$description: The table itself, in the shape ui.md §3.5 records: the element IS the box, a CSS table with the table role, and never a wrapper round a native one. Its rows are its own children, because a slot leaves no node and a mapped array leaves only a comment, so a slice of rows is still a table. It is the static table pattern, not the grid: it takes no focus and has no keyboard.

label.description: The accessible name of the table, written as aria-label. A table is announced by its name when a reader enters it, and nothing lints its absence, because a role-carrying custom element is outside the naming rules. Empty writes no attribute.

rowcount.description: How many rows the WHOLE set has, the header row included, written as aria-rowcount. It is for a table that draws only the rows in view: without it a reader is told the table has as many rows as happen to be rendered. Zero, the default, writes nothing, which is how a table that draws every row says count me from the DOM. The element prints what it is given; the host does the counting.
